newsitem.title: THAILAND: IFCT buys 18 pct of Thai bank shares.
newsitem.headline: IFCT buys 18 pct of Thai bank shares.

text.p: The Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) said on Thursday it plans to buy 18 percent of troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc's outstanding equity at 10 baht a share as part of its agreement to help manage the bank.

IFCT president Aswin Kongsiri told reporters his industrial financing bank would pay an initial amount of about 320 million baht ($12.3 million) for five percent of the value of the bank's shares that it would acquire.
He said the remaining 95 percent payment would be made in tranches between the third and seventh year of its management.
Aswin declined to say how much his firm would pay for the entire 18 percent stake in the bank.
He said IFCT would buy the stake from the Financial Institutions Development Fund, a central bank unit that currently owns about 65 percent of the bank's equity.
The government took over the bank last May after disclosure in parliament that it was saddled with about 78 billion baht of non-performing loans.

IFCT has accepted a government request to help manage the troubled bank for seven years. IFCT nominees are expected to start running the bank from May 1 after current bank shareholders approve the new management team.

Aswin said the initial five percent payment for the BBC shares would not affect IFCT's earnings. He said payment for the rest of the shares would partly be made with the management fee revenue that IFCT would earn for running the bank.
